claims.hypothesis: Extended velocity features (EVFs) analogous to those in the Milky Way exist in the bar dust lanes of external barred galaxies.
claims.experiment: Constructed CO(2-1) PP and PV diagnostic maps for 29 CO-barred galaxies and 13 unbarred control galaxies from PHANGS-ALMA and visually searched for compact, broad-lined features along the dust lanes.
claims.result: Identified 18 EVFs across 10 of the 29 barred galaxies (34%), with masses of 10^5-10^6 M_sun, radii of ~100 pc, and FWHM velocity spreads of 27-73 km s^-1, whereas unbarred galaxies generally lack EVFs (only 1 tentative case in 13 galaxies).
claims.finding: EVFs exist in external barred galaxies with physical properties analogous to Milky Way EVFs and are strongly linked to barred potentials.

evidence.quote: After examining the PP and PV diagrams of the 29 galaxies in our sample, we identified EVFs in 10 out of 29 galaxies, which represents approximately 34% of the total.
However, the general absence of EVF signatures in unbarred galaxies supports the argument that EVFs arise primarily due to cloud-cloud or stream-stream collisions in bar lanes.

claims.hypothesis: EVFs are strongly out-of-equilibrium structures produced by extreme cloud-cloud or stream-stream collisions in bar-driven non-circular flows.
claims.experiment: Measured the sizes, velocity dispersions, CO masses, and virial parameters of the 18 identified EVFs, and inspected PHANGS-JWST 7.7 um images for low-surface-density gas streams.
claims.result: All 18 EVFs have virial parameters ranging from 76 to 2925 (mostly a few hundred to several thousand), and 9 of the 18 EVFs show faint 7.7 um gas streams extending from the opposite side of the bar to the EVF location.
claims.finding: EVFs are highly unbound systems most likely originating from extreme collisions between dust-lane gas streams and overshooting streams from the opposite bar end.

evidence.quote: Upon analysing the physical properties of the EVFs, we find they possess large virial parameters, ranging from few hundreds to several thousand, indicating that they are strongly out-of-equilibrium.

Upon examining the 7.7 µm band observations of all galaxies with EVFs, we find that out of 18 EVF regions, 9 are associated with faint streams extending from the opposite end of the bar toward the EVF location.

claims.hypothesis: The velocity extent of EVFs is driven purely by the planar bulk velocity difference of colliding clouds rather than isotropic turbulent dispersion.
claims.experiment: Tested for a correlation between Delta v and galaxy inclination sin(i), and tested whether Delta v / sin(i) shows a minimum when the bar is aligned with the line of nodes (PA_LON - PA_bar = 0).
claims.result: Delta v shows a rough positive trend with sin(i) with large scatter, but Delta v / sin(i) shows no clear minimum at PA_LON = PA_bar.
claims.finding: While the planar velocity difference between colliding clouds contributes to Delta v, turbulent random motions generated by the collision also contribute significantly.

evidence.quote: The figure shows a rough correlation between ∆v and sin(i), consistent with expectations for the EVF velocity extent resulting from velocity difference of the colliding clouds.

There is no clear minimum at PALON = PAbar. This may indicate that turbulent random motions resulting from the collision significantly contribute to the velocity extent of EVFs, which therefore is not solely caused by the velocity difference of the colliding clouds.

limitations_admitted.value: Visual identification and contour enclosure of dust lanes and circular EVF regions in glue is somewhat subjective.

evidence.quote: While this procedure is somewhat subjective, the results are reasonable, as the dust lanes are typically coherent and continuous structures in PP space.

limitations_admitted.value: 2D Gaussian fitting overestimates the physical radius R_EVF (and thus virial parameter) for unresolved EVFs, so R_EVF values are upper limits.

evidence.quote: We note that this procedure will overestimate the radius of unresolved EVFs, so the radii should be considered upper limits.

We caveat that if the EVFs are unresolved in the PHANGS-ALMA CO data (which is possible given their ‘blobby’ appearance), then we will overestimate their virial parameter since REVF will be larger than the true cloud size.

limitations_admitted.value: Parameter uncertainties only reflect covariance matrix fitting errors and do not account for non-Gaussian intensity distributions, overlapping contaminating features, or spatial resolution limits.

evidence.quote: These uncertainties reflect the confidence intervals in the fitting only and they do not take into account that the shape of the intensity distribution within EVF region might be non-Gaussian, that there might be contaminating emission from other features overlapping with the EVF in PP space, or that the radius can be overestimated when the EVF is unresolved.

limitations_admitted.value: Adopting a constant Galactic alpha_CO ignores galaxy-scale variations and likely overestimates M_CO (underestimating alpha_vir) in high-velocity-dispersion central/bar regions.

evidence.quote: We adopt this procedure for simplicity, but note that it ignores galaxy-scale variations (e.g. den Brok et al. 2025) and might overestimate the mass for high-velocity dispersion features such as the EVF since high velocity dispersion often causes lower αCO values near galactic centres (Teng et al. 2023).

limitations_admitted.value: Spatial resolution is insufficient to conclusively determine whether EVFs lie on the leading or trailing edge of thin dust lanes.

evidence.quote: Although it is difficult to assess this conclusively as dust lanes are thin and the spatial resolution is not sufficient to examine this in detail, some galaxies appear consistent with this expectation (e.g. NGC 1512, NGC 2903, NGC 3627), but for some other galaxies the EVFs seem to occur on the leading side of the bar lanes (e.g. NGC 1097 and NGC 4535).

referee_caveats_inferred: EVF selection is entirely visual and lacks an quantitative, automated detection threshold in PPV space (e.g. a minimum line width or brightness contrast relative to the surrounding dust lane).

Because the spatial resolution of PHANGS-ALMA (50-180 pc) is comparable to the derived EVF radii (70-150 pc), beam smearing of steep velocity gradients across the bar shock could artificially broaden the spectra without requiring distinct colliding streams.
The JWST 7.7 um PAH emission lacks kinematic information, so the physical association and inflow direction of the visually traced streams hitting the EVFs cannot be kinematically confirmed.

reproducibility.score_reason: All underlying ALMA and JWST high-level datacubes and images are publicly available via CANFAR and MAST, and the mathematical equations for radii, masses, and virial parameters are explicitly given. However, the dust lane masks and initial circular EVF apertures were drawn manually in glue without publishing the exact region coordinates or aperture sizes, though the diagnostic plots and R_cen values allow approximate localization.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: The PHANGS-ALMA cubes are publicly available, the 18 EVFs are visually marked in the paper's figures with galactocentric radii and physical properties tabulated in Table 2, and the Gaussian fitting and virial equations are straightforward to re-implement.
